# Ferdinand Lauren — The Systems Workbench

Computer Science undergraduate at Universitas Lampung (2022 cohort), based in Bandar Lampung,
Indonesia. Building towards IT business analysis and ERP functional consulting.

Positioning: entry-level. No industry experience claimed.

Working sequence: observe → define → design → verify. It is a personal working approach,
practised on one independent concept project and on coursework — not a methodology validated in
client engagements.

## What this site contains

- Two in-depth case studies.
- GYM-QR: a self-initiated gym attendance and locker management concept. It is documented as a
  concept, not client work. Includes a 1,166-line PRD, two state machines, 15 acceptance scenarios,
  and 130 passing automated tests in the source repository.
- Procure-to-Pay: an independent learning case study set in a fictional distributor. It documents
  a purchase request → approval → order → goods receipt → invoice verification → payment process,
  with 9 business rules, 12 functional requirements and 10 acceptance criteria. No ERP product was
  configured and no business outcome is claimed.
- The Decision Lab: four documented decision cases from the GYM-QR system, with the initial conditions,
  the rules, the decision trace, the expected result, edge cases, and the evidence level for each.
- The AI Workbench: AI positioned as a drafting tool inside a reviewed workflow. It claims no
  time saving, no productivity metric, and no specific requirement written by a model.
- Coursework: Prak_WebLanjut, wuish, UAS-DSP, DSP, BMI_Calculator, pastebin. Labelled as coursework.

## Pages

- / — the desk, working approach, featured case file, Decision Lab, AI Workbench, selected work,
  about and contact
- /work/gym-qr — the GYM-QR case study as a document: observe, analyse, define, verify, reflect
- /work/p2p-procurement — the Procure-to-Pay learning case study: context, process, actors, rules,
  requirements, acceptance criteria, exceptions, ERP concepts, scope
